name: Faisalabad International Airport
notes: paa.gov.pk is a JavaScript app; deep links (e.g. https://paa.gov.pk/airport/faisalabad/services/prayer-rooms) return HTTP 404 when loaded directly. The Faisalabad airport portal content was read on 18 Oct 2026 from the site's own public content API (official PAA domain, key embedded in the site's JavaScript), the source cited. Its "Prayer Rooms" service entry (front-end path /services/prayer-rooms under portal /airport/faisalabad) says: "Muslim prayer rooms and ablution areas/rooms are available throughout the airport for women and men." This is the same standard text used on other PAA airport portals; no terminal, side, hours or count is given. The portal also has a "Complaint & Feedback" / E-Complaint section (path /procedure/complaints-feedback), but no directly loadable URL was found, so feedback_url is unknown. Not visually verified.

notes: Official Gan International Airport (Addu International Airport Pvt Ltd) Departures Guide https://ganairport.com/depatures.html fetched directly 18 Oct 2026. Quote: "Once the security check is complete and if you are a domestic passenger proceed to the Domestic Departure Hall ... In the Departure Hall toilets and a Prayer Room is available." and, for international passengers after Passport Control, "proceed to the International Departure Hall ... In the Departure Hall toilets and a Prayer Room is available." Side is from that sequence (after security). The site's other 39 linked pages (arrivals, services, travel guide) were fetched and do not mention prayer. No feedback page was found (phone +960 689 8010 only). Scheduled Maldivian flights shown on the site for 18 Oct 2026. Not visually verified.

name: Hanimaadhoo International Airport
notes: Secondary only. Airport Technology project profile (published 26 Apr 2023, read directly 18 Oct 2026) on the Hanimaadhoo redevelopment says the new passenger terminal "will also feature modern facilities and amenities such as VIP waiting lounges, prayer rooms, seating areas and baby care facilities." This was written before the terminal opened (operations moved to the new terminal in Oct 2025 per edition.mv), so the prayer rooms are a planned feature not confirmed after opening. No official operator facilities page was found (macl.aero covers Velana only). Maldivian news articles on the opening (edition.mv, atolltimes.mv, psmnews.mv) were fetched and do not mention prayer facilities. Not visually verified.

name: Brunei International Airport

spaces.name: Airport Surau (prayer hall)
spaces.location: Separate building "in the vicinity of the new Brunei International Airport Terminal", on a raised platform

notes: Secondary only (news). The Borneo Post, 29 Apr 2014 (reporting BruDirect), read via its Wayback capture of 5 Jun 2021 because the live page is behind a Cloudflare challenge: the Ministry of Communications and BEDB laid the foundation for "the new Surau (Prayer Hall) for the Brunei International Airport ... The Surau located in the vicinity of the new Brunei International Airport Terminal will provide Muslim worshippers with an additional and better praying facility in addition to the existing prayer rooms available in the Airport Terminal ... can be seen by both departing and arriving passengers ... will accommodate at least 300 worshippers and is expected to be completed by the end of November 2014." Completion was not confirmed by a later source; the surau side is INFERENCE (separate building outside the terminal). The article is 12 years old. No official airport website was found (bruneiairport.com is a parked travel-search domain; dca.gov.bn site search for surau/prayer returns nothing). Not visually verified.
